gap: No result ChatGPT got states how large an image each projector can throw and still reach 40 foot-lamberts, the level for a lit office. From each maker's rated lumens, the Nebula Capsule 3 Laser reaches it only up to about a 50-inch diagonal (15.8 fL at 80 inches). The Epson CO-FH02, CO-W01 and PowerLite 1781W reach it up to about 155–160 inches (150–160 fL at 80 inches).
standout_why: Beecommercer (cited) lists rated lumens (300 ANSI for the Capsule 3 Laser, 3,000 for the CO-FH02) and works out throw distances (2.13 m for an 80-inch image at a 1.2 ratio). It also says it does not 'calculate a brightness multiple between these products', and it gives no foot-lamberts, nits or largest usable size for a lit room. TechRadar's page came back truncated with no product text. Rottenwifi (cited) timed out twice, so I could not check it. ChatGPT's own answer only says the Capsule's 300 lumens make it 'better suited to dark rooms', with no number for screen brightness or size.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's choice of the Epsons for presentations and puts a number on the pocket-versus-backpack follow-up question. In a lit office the Capsule 3 Laser works only on a TV-sized image of about 50 inches. Any of the three Epsons can fill a 100-inch wall at about 60 fL or more. Per pound, the 1781W (800 lm/lb, 4.0 lb, $899.99 at Epson) is the best travel pick for lit rooms. For lit rooms the CO-W01 costs least per lumen ($133 per 1,000 lm), but its resolution is WXGA.

findings.label: Screen brightness targets and formula
findings.value: 16–26 ftL dark room; 40–59 ftL medium ambient (offices, classrooms); 60+ ftL high ambient; ftL = (lumens ÷ screen area ft²) × gain
findings.source_title: What are Foot-Lamberts and Why Do I Care? (ProjectorScreen.com)
findings.note: These are ProjectorScreen.com's bands. All math below uses a 1.0-gain screen and the makers' rated lumens, not measured lumens.
